Where it began

Kusal Mendis was born in Moratuwa on 2 February 1995. He went to Prince of Wales' College in his home town and captained the school side, and in 2013 he was named Sri Lanka's schoolboy cricketer of the year. A year later he led his country at the Under-19 World Cup.

Things moved fast after that. He had played only 16 first-class matches when Sri Lanka gave him his Test cap in 2015, against West Indies, as their 132nd Test player.

The player

By November 2026 he had played 76 Tests and made 4,955 runs at 36.98, with 11 hundreds, 23 fifties and a best of 245. He was useful with the gloves too, with 41 catches and five stumpings as wicketkeeper on top of 86 catches in the field.

The first big day came at Pallekele in July 2016, when his maiden Test hundred against Australia set up a win by 106 runs, only Sri Lanka's second in Tests against them. In 2018 he made 1,023 Test runs in the calendar year, and in New Zealand he and Angelo Mathews batted through an entire day and helped secure a draw. Soon after, at Port Elizabeth, his unbeaten fifty finished off a series win in South Africa, something no Asian side had managed before. His double hundred, 245 against Ireland in 2023, came with 11 sixes. And in November 2026, leading Sri Lanka for the first time in a Test, against Pakistan, he made a hundred. No Sri Lankan had marked a first Test in charge that way before.

What made him special

He liked to get on with it. Against New Zealand in 2023 he raced to a Test fifty and went on to 87 from 83 balls. He also had a rare knack of falling just short of 200: twice he was out in the 190s, a habit he shares with Kumar Sangakkara, which is decent company for a near miss.

His one-day game had the same freedom. Against India in the 2017 Champions Trophy his 89 helped Sri Lanka chase 321, then the highest successful chase in that tournament. In 2024 he made 143 against New Zealand, his best in one-day cricket.

Away from the middle

Sri Lanka Cricket named him its one-day batsman of the year for 2016–17. He led the one-day side during the 2023 World Cup, including a fine win over England, and played franchise cricket in Sri Lanka and South Africa, where he was player of the match for Pretoria Capitals with 80 from 41 balls.

And finally

He came into Test cricket with so few first-class games behind him that he did much of his learning in the toughest school there is. By the time he was captain, the pupil had become the head teacher.
